page: Microsoft Azure GS4-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2698B v3 processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs, with 1.0 thread per core. It is equipped with 224.0 GB of system memory, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 56.0 GB per core. Additionally, the instance includes 459 GB of local storage and does not feature any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between massive memory capacity and processing throughput. The Intel Xeon E5-2698B v3 processor delivers poor single-core and multi-core CPU performance, placing in the bottom 10% of stress-ng benchmarks. Similarly, Geekbench and Passmark CPU scores fall into the weak category. While small-block cached memory read bandwidth is average, large-block uncached memory write bandwidth is poor at 14.26 GB/sec. This indicates that while the server can hold large datasets in memory, intensive computational tasks and heavy memory write operations will experience performance bottlenecks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the GS4-4 offers high resource density specifically for memory-bound applications, allowing users to avoid provisioning higher vCPU counts just to obtain substantial RAM. However, the low compute-to-memory ratio makes it inefficient for CPU-heavy tasks. This server is best suited for memory-intensive workloads with low CPU demands, such as large-scale in-memory caching, database operations with moderate transaction rates, and legacy enterprise applications requiring significant memory footprints without parallel processing needs.
